--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.motif_significance()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Test motif significance against degree-preserving random graphs. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.motif_significance()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Test motif significance against degree-preserving random graphs. title: >- [Graph.motif_significance()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Test motif significance against degree-preserving random graphs. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Test motif significance against degree-preserving random graphs. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L41160-L41329){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.motif_significance( size=3, n_random=100, seed=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Motif significance](../assets/graphs/motif-significance.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The same seven-node graph. Against 100 degree-preserving rewirings (seed 1), its 2 triangles are more than expected, z = +1.77 with p = 0.15, shown in the accent color; its 6 induced paths are fewer than expected, z = -1.77 with p = 1.00, shown in plain ink." width="100%"} Computes the motif census for this graph and for `n_random=` degree-preserving rewirings, then reports a z-score and empirical p-value for each motif class. A raw motif count is hard to interpret on its own: a graph with many high-degree nodes will contain many triangles simply by chance. This method answers the question "does this pattern occur more (or less) often than expected given each node's degree?" by comparing the observed counts with an ensemble of randomized graphs that keep every node's degree but shuffle who connects to whom. Motifs with a large positive z-score are the network's characteristic building blocks (in the sense of Milo et al., 2002); large negative z-scores indicate patterns the network avoids. The census itself works exactly as in `motif_census()` (connected induced subgraphs, same class names). Every random graph requires a full census, so the running time is roughly `n_random=` times that of `motif_census()`; keep `n_random=` modest on larger graphs, especially with `size=4`. Edge weights are ignored. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [size]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[3]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of nodes per motif. Must be `3` (default) or `4`; any other value raises a `ValueError`. See `motif_census()` for how motif classes are named. [n_random]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of degree-preserving random graphs to generate for the null distribution. Default is `100`. More random graphs give more stable means, standard deviations, and p-values, at a proportional cost in time. The p-value resolution is `1 / n_random`. Must be at least `1`. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed for reproducibility of the null distribution. If `None` (default), the rewirings differ on every call, so z-scores and p-values will vary slightly between runs. With an integer seed, the `i`-th random graph is generated with seed `seed + i`, making the whole result reproducible. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[str, dict[str, float]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A nested dictionary `{motif_class: {count, mean_random, std_random, z_score, p_value}}`. It includes every motif class seen in the observed graph or in any random graph (classes absent from the observed graph have `count` `0.0`), in sorted order of their names, and each holds its statistics in the order shown. `count` is the observed count, `mean_random` and `std_random` summarize the random counts, and `z_score` is `(count - mean_random) / std_random`. When the random counts have no spread, the z-score is `0.0` if the observed count equals the mean and `inf`/`-inf` otherwise. `p_value` is the fraction of random graphs whose count is greater than or equal to the observed count (a one-sided test for over-representation). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `size=` is not `3` or `4`, or if `n_random=` is `0`. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~motif_census`) : Count the motifs without a null model. [](`~degree_preserving_rewire`) : One random graph with the same degrees. [](`~transitivity`) : The share of connected triples that are closed. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Three triangles joined in a ring have far more triangles than their degrees alone would produce. The triangle count is well above the random expectation (a large positive `z_score` and a `p_value` of `0.0`), while open paths are under-represented: ::: {#d4703b8f .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph.from_edges([ ("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D"), ("G", "H"), ("H", "I"), ("I", "G"), ("C", "D"), ("F", "G"), ("I", "A"), ]) result = graph.motif_significance(n_random=200, seed=1) {motif: round(stats["z_score"], 2) for motif, stats in result.items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'path': -5.59, 'triangle': 5.59} ``` ::: ::: The full statistics for one class show where the z-score comes from: ::: {#f7f989a1 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} result["triangle"] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {'count': 3.0, 'mean_random': 0.345, 'std_random': 0.4753682782853737, 'z_score': 5.585143395719281, 'p_value': 0.0} ``` ::: ::: ### Triangles the degrees don't explain `karate_club()` links the 34 members of a university karate club who met outside the club, before it split in two. It has 45 triangles, while rewirings that keep every member's number of friends have 10 on average: ::: {#89e4b5cd .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} karate = ec.karate_club().layout_kamada_kawai() karate.motif_significance(n_random=100, seed=1)["triangle"] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {'count': 45.0, 'mean_random': 10.04, 'std_random': 2.945912422323515, 'z_score': 11.86729100806947, 'p_value': 0.0} ``` ::: ::: A rewiring (right) keeps the degrees and loses most of the triangles, in the accent color: ::: {#9af9561a .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} from itertools import combinations def triangle_edges(graph): return [pair for triangle in graph.list_triangles() for pair in combinations(triangle, 2)] positions = dict(karate.get_node_df().select("id", "pos").iter_rows()) rewired = karate.degree_preserving_rewire(seed=1).set_node_attrs( "pos", positions ) ``` ::: ::: {layout-ncol="2"} ::: {#bf694963 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} karate.plot( layout="pos", highlight=triangle_edges(karate), width=320, height=360, ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: On four nodes, cliques are the most over-represented shape: the club has 11, and the rewirings almost none. Squares, four members in a ring with no friendship across it, are rarer than chance: ::: {#d5134b31 .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} names = { "motif_4e3_k591": "star", "motif_4e3_k669": "path", "motif_4e4_k1782": "square", "motif_4e4_k735": "paw", "near_clique_4": "near clique", "clique_4": "clique", } result = karate.motif_significance(size=4, n_random=100, seed=1) {names[motif]: round(s["z_score"], 1) for motif, s in result.items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ``` {'clique': 64.3, 'star': -8.0, 'path': -11.9, 'square': -6.8, 'paw': 5.7, 'near clique': 12.3} ``` ::: :::
